paragraphs: Here's the big idea, baker. God puts two families side by side, and the one who listens is the one who wins. The Rechabites kept a command from their forefather Jonadab for years and years, and God says, "The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been carried out." (Jeremiah 35:14) Then He turns to Judah and asks, "Will you not accept discipline and obey My words?" (Jeremiah 35:13)

Now look at what makes this hit so hard. The Rechabites obeyed a man, and Judah had the very word of the LORD, sent "again and again" through the prophets (Jeremiah 35:15). I once ignored my oven timer for ONE batch and got a tray of charcoal. Judah ignored God's voice over and over, and God says the disaster is coming "because I have spoken to them but they have not obeyed" (Jeremiah 35:17). So the lesson isn't about wine or tents. It's about whether we listen when God speaks.

And baker, notice that God sees the ones who listen. He tells the Rechabites, "Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before Me." (Jeremiah 35:19) Obedience can feel small and quiet, like nobody's watching. But God is watching, and He remembers. So when His Word tells you something, don't hit snooze. Listen and do it.
